messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated error rate detected for /v1/generate in prod-us-west-2. p95 latency from 1.2s -> 4.8s; p99 from 2.1s -> 9.1s. 5xx rate increased to 5.1%. Deploy finished ~4m ago.

maya: saw the alert on the dashboard. deploy just finished, right?

deploy-bot: deploy r2026.3 -> prod-us-west-2 completed at +240s. Owner: runtime-team.

aj: I’m oncall — I’ll take it. grabbing traces and logs. can someone snapshot the console dashboards?

katie: grabbing logs from edge gateways now. early signs show a lot of `gateway: upstream_timeout` and `kvcache evict` messages.

sergio: throwing a quick grep on runtime logs — large clumps of `kv_cache_eviction: padding=1.2s` around the same time as the deploy. suspicious.

linh: that padding change was part of the kernel tweaks in r2026.3 (memory-affinity + new kernel selector). Might be causing more frequent evictions under certain seq lengths.

aj: can you paste a few logs?

sergio: ```
[2026-03-15T12:45:02Z] model=llama-large req_id=abc123 latency=812ms state=serving kv_cache_eviction=true padding_ms=1200
[2026-03-15T12:45:02Z] model=llama-large req_id=abc124 error=upstream_timeout code=504 backend_wait=9000ms
[2026-03-15T12:45:03Z] model=llama-large req_id=abc125 latency=920ms state=cache_miss
```

maya: that 9s backend_wait lines are definitely the p99s. are we seeing this across models or just the big ones?

katie: mostly the larger decoder models, traffic spike on long-seq chat routes. smaller embed routes look fine.

aj: consensus: r2026.3 introduced a kernel selection/config that increases KV eviction frequency for long sequences -> spikes backend wait -> 5xx/timeouts. we should roll back immediately.

linh: agree. rollback to r2026.2 is the safest. I’ll prep the rollback command.

aj: go for it. execute and announce.

linh: executing rollback: `./deploy rollback --env prod-us-west-2 --from r2026.3 --to r2026.2 --reason "p99 timeout regression"`

deploy-bot: rollback job started by linh. job id 987654. rolling out r2026.2 -> prod-us-west-2.

maya: I’m updating the incident channel and paging customers with potential impact.

aj: monitoring metrics now — watch p95/p99 and 5xx. also enabling automatic fallback to smaller model variant for chat route as a short-term mitigation.

katie: added a route-level fallback: `route: /chat -> fallback: llama-medium` (enabled).

[~2 minutes later]

incident-bot: UPDATE: rollback job 987654 progress: 60% -> 90% nodes updated. error rate trending down: 5xx 5.1% -> 1.4%. p99 9.1s -> 2.4s.

aj: seeing connection stats normalize on frontends. p95 back near baseline. good sign.

sergio: retention logs show fewer `kv_cache_eviction` spikes post-rollback.

linh: rollback completed. deploy-bot: rollback job 987654 finished. r2026.2 is live.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: rollback complete.

maya: great. I’ve notified affected customers with a note: transient errors/timeouts from 12:44–12:52 UTC, rollback mitigated. Support ticket created: INC-2026-588.

aj: for immediate tasks: 1) alert runtime team to revert the kvcache padding change and open a PR with more canary/test coverage; 2) add a short-term routing policy to avoid large seq routing to single kernel; 3) schedule postmortem.

linh: created GH issue runtime#462: "revert/adjust kernel selector padding — investigate kvcache eviction behavior". assigning to runtime owners.

katie: leaving a note for SRE-runbooks: update rollback checklist to include fallback route trigger for chat routes.

maya: handoff: aj — please create the incident timeline and assign to morning oncall for follow-up (owner: sergio + lin h).

aj: will do. timeline + initial blameless postmortem draft in INC-2026-588.

incident-bot: SEVERITY: P1 -> downgraded to P2; customer impact: partial (high latency/timeouts for a subset of long-seq traffic).

sergio: quick postmortem notes: root cause likely regression in kernel selection/padding that increased kvcache eviction frequency for long sequences under the current workload, leading to heavy backend waits and gateway timeouts.

maya: thanks all. closing incident channel for now — keep the ticket open for follow-up. :thumbsup:

aj: handoff done. oncall until 08:00 UTC tomorrow will own follow-ups.

katie: adding mitigation checklist to INC-2026-588.

linh: will run an extended canary with synthetic long-seq tests before reintroducing the change.

maya: file synchronized. good job everyone. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
